about.title: Who writes this blog
about.lead: Oussama Abid. He left Oujda, learned in Grenoble, and builds Krizaka in Montréal.
about.slot: The Krizaka mark, until there is a photo
body: My name is Oussama, and I come from Oujda, in Morocco.

In 2010 I left to study in Grenoble. Mathematics and computer science applied to the social sciences first, then a master's with a rather long name: cognition, creation and learning engineering. Put simply, how we think, how we learn, and what a machine can do with that.

In 2011 I did my first research internship at the LIG, Grenoble's computer science lab, in natural language processing. Teaching a machine to read a sentence, pull out the facts, get at the meaning. Nobody talked about AI at parties back then. That's still where I started.

Then fifteen years building systems that run for real. Connected trains, healthcare apps for a hospital, mobile platforms for telecom operators, connected cities with millions of devices. Then banking platforms, when I arrived in Montréal in 2019.

Today I'm an architect at a large Canadian bank. And on the side I build Krizaka, here in Montréal, with AI agents that I direct, review and correct. It comes full circle, a little: I met the machine that reads a sentence in Grenoble, and now I put it to work.
When I'm not coding, I listen to jazz, go to concerts, travel when I can, and keep a game controller within reach.
This blog is what I learn while building. Short posts, with the numbers I can show, and what I haven't solved yet.
about.homeBody: My name is Oussama. I left Oujda, learned in Grenoble, and build Krizaka in Montréal. My first brush with AI was in 2011, in a research lab, long before the word was in fashion. Here I tell what I learn along the way.
